jobs.rawPrompt: Scientific educational correction of the supplied friendly pastel image for a German Gymnasium learner: interpret ion formation through one-electron transfer and stable noble-gas shell occupation. PNG, landscape 16:9 about 1600×900. The old countable ring drawings are scientifically wrong and cannot be retained. Replace ONLY those false shell drawings with a clearly labelled symbolic particle-and-occupation model WITHOUT any ring drawings and WITHOUT electron dots to be counted. Keep the friendly soft blue sodium and green chlorine colour language, rounded panels and short correct equations. Simple spacious comic arrangement: TOP row large rounded symbols 'Na' and 'Cl', with a clear orange 'e⁻' transfer arrow pointing FROM Na TO Cl. Under Na the large exact shell-occupation label '2 | 8 | 1', under Cl '2 | 8 | 7'. BOTTOM row large symbols 'Na⁺' and 'Cl⁻', reached by down arrows from their corresponding initial atoms; under Na⁺ exact '2 | 8', under Cl⁻ exact '2 | 8 | 8'. Na⁺ caption 'Kation', Cl⁻ caption 'Anion'. Title only 'Ionenbildung'; short legend 'Schalenbelegung' so the occupation numbers are explicit. The symbols are schematic particles, not molecular drawings; no faces or nuclei, no uncounted decorative dot clouds. A single transferred electron does not create or change the atomic nucleus. Outer occupation 8 on both product ions is visibly highlighted with a soft yellow halo around the corresponding numeral, never additional electron dots. The numbers and charge signs must be large and readable at 360-pixel width. Friendly, abstract and inviting, no photorealism, no sterile technical chart, no tiny lesson text or watermark or technical IDs. Scope is clearly the example Na/Cl, not a universal claim about every ion or element.
jobs.altText: Natrium mit Schalenbelegung 2|8|1 gibt ein Elektron an Chlor mit 2|8|7 ab. Es entstehen das Kation Na⁺ mit 2|8 und das Anion Cl⁻ mit 2|8|8; die Außenschalen sind voll.

jobs.rawPrompt: Scientific educational correction for the supplied German NaCl lattice-energy illustration. Output friendly abstract comic-style PNG, wide 16:9 about 1600×900, restrained pastel blue/green, rounded hand-drawn outlines, clear sparse German labels readable at 360-pixel width. The original false shell-electron dot graphics MUST be removed entirely. Use symbolic particles WITHOUT electron dots or rings; explicit shell occupation labels are allowed. Show a large clean QUALITATIVE ENERGY LANDSCAPE in three steps, with upward energy axis on left: initial lower-middle level 'Na(s) + ½ Cl₂(g)' represented by a grey metal cube and a small separate two-green-circle chlorine molecule. Middle gaseous-ion level MUST be ABOVE this initial level and labelled 'Na⁺(g) + Cl⁻(g)': separated blue Na⁺ and green Cl⁻ symbols with short occupation labels '2|8' and '2|8|8'. A short orange arrow UP from initial to middle says 'Vorbereitung: Energiezufuhr'. Then a much larger blue/green arrow DOWN to final crystalline level 'NaCl(s)' BELOW the INITIAL baseline: friendly square section of an extended checkerboard lattice with alternating blue '+' and green '−' ions, equal positive and negative counts, NO covalent bond sticks and no discrete NaCl molecule. Down arrow says 'Gitterbildung: Energiefreisetzung'. Main large bottom label 'insgesamt exotherm: ΔH < 0'. The neutral element stage, gaseous-ion stage and crystalline-solid stage must remain distinct; positive activation/preparation then greater exothermic lattice release gives lower final energy. No absolute energy values and no claim that electron attachment itself costs energy. Preserve the core correct scientific meaning of the existing energy diagram while replacing its demonstrably incorrect atomic-shell pictures with symbolic schematic particles. No photorealism, no sterile grid/chart, no small paragraph text, no technical IDs or watermark.
jobs.altText: Schematischer Energieverlauf der Bildung von NaCl: Die Vorbereitung von Natrium und Chlor zu gasförmigen Na⁺- und Cl⁻-Ionen kostet netto Energie. Die anschließende Gitterbildung setzt mehr Energie frei; NaCl liegt energetisch tiefer und die Gesamtänderung ist exotherm.
